response: Yes, overexpression of Ki-67 is considered a prognostic biomarker of upper tract urinary carcinoma. Ki-67 is a nuclear protein that is expressed in proliferating cells, and its overexpression has been associated with tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis in various types of cancer, including upper tract urinary carcinoma. Studies have shown that high Ki-67 expression levels are correlated with higher tumor grades, increased risk of recurrence, and shorter overall survival rates in patients with upper tract urinary carcinoma. Therefore, Ki-67 can be used as a prognostic biomarker to help predict patient outcomes and guide treatment decisions.
